description: Phase-OP — Aura learns from her own mistakes without user-in-the-loop. Discovered live 2026-05-18T19:22-19:36 in Telegram convo (chat_id=1148481707): user explicitly asked 'Ma come te lo segni?' and Aura answered 'Non posso scrivere direttamente — la policy dice propose_patch action=operational' which goes to review queue, user mobile can't approve, loop blocked. Aura ammette che propose_patch in review e' 'cafonata' ma il fix in TOOLS.md non basta perche' la policy e' hard-coded, non in prompt. Plus 3 distinct tool-call errors in 10 min (list_files path outside root, propose_patch missing change_summary, file missing action) prove she doesn't retain mistake-recovery cross-turn. Five stories make her loop-autonomous: skip review for operational self-talk, persist+retrieve operational lessons, inject top-10 in system prompt overlay, reload overlay mid-conversation, infer missing file action. After Phase-OP: Aura impara veramente, daily-use Telegram funziona senza PC approval. Each story = single atomic commit on master per memory feedback_one_module_per_slice.

userStories.title: propose_patch action=operational auto-accepts — skip review queue
userStories.description: Currently propose_patch action=operational writes to proposed_updates with status=pending. User must approve via dashboard before the lesson lands anywhere retrievable. Aura is mobile-blocked. Fix: kind=operational auto-accepts (writes directly to the operational store, skipping review). Keep kind=user_memory unchanged (still requires human review). (a) Find the propose_patch handler in internal/api/ or internal/learning/ (search for 'proposed_updates' table writes). (b) Branch on kind: operational -> write directly to compact_memory_documents kind=operational AND/OR data/operational_lessons.md. user_memory -> keep status=pending review flow. (c) Migration: existing rows in proposed_updates with kind=operational and status=pending -> auto-accept them. (d) Tests: insert operational proposal -> assert status=accepted immediately + a row appears in compact_memory_documents kind=operational. user_memory proposal -> status=pending unchanged.

userStories.title: Top-N operational lessons injected in system prompt overlay each conversation
userStories.description: Even with US-OP02 (recall_operational finds lessons), Aura must REMEMBER to call it. Better: inject top-10 most recent operational lessons in system prompt overlay so Aura sees them every turn without explicit tool call. (a) New prompt overlay OPS.md (sibling of SOUL/AGENT/USER/TOOLS.md) OR extend AGENT.md with 'Operational lessons' section. (b) At conversation start (hub.Receive boundary), prompt assembler queries compact_memory_documents kind=operational ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 10. (c) Cap at 5 KB total. (d) Test: seed 11 lessons, assert top 10 in system prompt sorted by recency.

userStories.title: Mid-conversation prompt overlay reload after file tool patches overlay files
userStories.description: Aura at 19:34:30 patched TOOLS.md to remove review-queue policy. At 19:35:00 she used propose_patch action=operational anyway because the new policy was invisible (system prompt cached from conversation start). Fix: when file tool patches an overlay file (SOUL.md, AGENT.md, USER.md, TOOLS.md, OPS.md), trigger reload so the next turn in the SAME conversation sees the updated overlay. (a) Detect overlay-file writes in the file tool Execute path. (b) Signal the agent loop to re-read overlays before the next LLM call. (c) Test: 2-turn probe — turn 1 patches TOOLS.md to say 'never use foo tool', turn 2 asks 'use foo tool' -> assistant refuses citing the new rule.

userStories.title: file tool action inference — recover from missing action without burning a turn
userStories.description: At 19:36:06 Aura called file({content:..., path:...}) without action. Tool returned a clear error 'looks like you meant write'. Aura recovered in 1 retry but burned a tool call. The error message already KNOWS the right inference — automate it. (a) In internal/agent/tools/registry/file.go, if action is missing, infer from arg shape: content+path -> write, only path -> read, pattern -> search, old+new+path -> patch. (b) Debug log: 'file: action inferred as X from arg shape'. (c) Ambiguous combinations still fail with clearer message. (d) Test: each inference case via unit test on Execute path.
